title: RBAC v2 feature-flag rollout plan: dual-read, staged enablement, and dashboards
creator: Connor O'Brien
content:
Goal
Implement a safe rollout mechanism for RBAC v2 across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments using:
1) feature flags + staged rollout controls
2) dual-read/compare mode (RBAC v1 and v2 evaluated in parallel)
3) dashboards + alerting for deny spikes, decision diffs, and latency regressions

Context
RBAC v2 is deny-by-default and relies on permission annotations + policy bundle definitions. We need a controlled migration path that lets us detect mismatches (v1 would allow, v2 would deny), avoid breaking customers during early adoption, and generate evidence-friendly telemetry for Security/GRC.

Scope
In-scope
- Feature flag definitions and config wiring in API Gateway + Control Plane services
- Dual-read mode (evaluate v1 + v2) and emit structured comparison metrics/events
- Rollout stages and per-scope override strategy (env/org/project/cluster as applicable)
- Dashboards + alerts (Datadog) + runbook updates for oncall and releases
- Dedicated/Private-specific defaults and operator guidance (e.g., Private installer bootstrap)

Out-of-scope
- Building new permissions or role templates themselves (covered by other tickets)
- Reworking authn/SSO flows

Proposed flags (names are draft; align final names with Platform config conventions)
Core flags
- rbac_v2.enable_enforcement: when true, RBAC v2 decisions are enforced (deny-by-default).
- rbac_v2.enable_dual_read: when true, evaluate v2 in parallel while enforcing v1 (or legacy checks) and emit diff telemetry.
- rbac_v2.enforcement_mode: one of ["v1_only", "dual_read_enforce_v1", "v2_only"].
- rbac_v2.fail_mode: one of ["fail_closed", "fail_open"] for evaluator errors/timeouts. Default differs by environment stage (see below).

Surface-specific flags
- rbac_v2.gateway_middleware_enabled: gate the gateway authz middleware path (global kill switch).
- rbac_v2.control_plane_interceptor_enabled: gate service-side interceptor enforcement.
- rbac_v2.console_admin_ux_enabled: gate Console role mgmt UI exposure (separate rollout track).

Debug / support flags
- rbac_v2.emit_denial_debug_headers_for_admins: controls exposure of debug headers (admin-only).
- rbac_v2.log_authz_decisions_sample_rate: sampling rate for decision logging beyond audit log requirements.

Decision: enforcement location + kill switches
- We will keep BOTH gateway and service-side switches. Services must not rely solely on gateway (defense-in-depth + internal callers).
- Global kill switch must allow immediate rollback to v1-only behavior without redeploy.

Dual-read design
Mechanics
- Request comes in; we compute:
  - legacy_decision (v1/coarse roles/legacy checks)
  - v2_decision (permission-based policy evaluation)
- In dual_read_enforce_v1 mode:
  - enforce legacy_decision
  - emit a diff record if legacy_decision != v2_decision OR if v2 returns "unknown" due to missing annotations/permission mapping
- In v2_only mode:
  - enforce v2_decision
  - still emit diff telemetry comparing against legacy (best-effort) for a limited window to catch unexpected allows/denies

Diff telemetry payload (structured)
- service (gateway/control-plane-service-name)
- route / rpc method
- action (permission string)
- scope (org/project/env/cluster ids where present; redact as needed)
- subject_type (user/api_key/service_token)
- legacy_decision (allow/deny)
- v2_decision (allow/deny/error/unknown)
- reason_code (for v2 denies; align with denial reason codes work)
- policy_version (bundle version/hash)

Important: unknown and missing-annotation handling
- If a request hits an endpoint without a permission annotation:
  - v2_decision = unknown
  - dual-read should emit a high-severity metric so we can gate rollout on “unknown rate” approaching zero for sensitive surfaces.

Failure modes
- Evaluator timeout / policy fetch error:
  - In prod initial phases: fail_open ONLY when in dual_read_enforce_v1 (since we’re not enforcing v2 anyway). Once v2_only begins, switch to fail_closed except for explicitly-approved break-glass paths.
  - Always emit error metrics.

Rollout stages (proposed)
Stage 0: Dev + CI
- Enable dual-read in dev/staging for all routes; enforce legacy.
- Gate merges with coverage checks where possible (e.g., no new sensitive endpoints without annotations).

Stage 1: Internal dogfood (Hosted)
- Target: Redwood internal orgs + admin accounts only.
- Mode: dual_read_enforce_v1
- Success criteria:
  - v2_unknown_rate < 0.1% of authz-evaluated requests for 24h
  - v1_allow_v2_deny_rate < 0.5% for 24h (with documented known gaps)
  - p95 authz evaluation overhead < 2ms gateway, < 3ms control plane services

Stage 2: Pilot customers (Dedicated + Private)
- Select 2–3 pilot accounts (coordinated by PM/SE), plus at least one Private install.
- Continue dual_read_enforce_v1 for 1–2 weeks, then flip to v2_only per-account.
- Ensure Private has straightforward rollback (config flag + documented procedure).

Stage 3: Gradual ramp (Hosted broad)
- Rollout v2_only by percentage of orgs, then by region.
- Keep gateway and service kill switches available for rapid revert.

Stage 4: Legacy deprecation
- After stable period (TBD; likely 60–90 days): disable dual-read metrics by default, keep only audit-required fields + minimal authz metrics.

Dashboards & alerts (Datadog)
Dashboards to create
1) RBAC v2 Rollout Overview
- total authz decisions/sec (by env, service)
- deny rate (v2) by route/permission
- v2_unknown_rate by service/route
- v1_allow_v2_deny_rate (diff) by permission
- v1_deny_v2_allow_rate (diff) by permission (watch for unintended privilege escalation)

2) Latency & errors
- evaluator latency (p50/p95/p99)
- cache hit rate for policy evaluator client
- evaluator error rate (timeouts, policy fetch failures)

3) Customer/pilot view
- allow/deny rates scoped to pilot org(s) / cluster(s)
- top denial reason codes

Alerts
- P0: v2_unknown_rate > 1% for 5m in prod while v2_only enabled anywhere
- P0: v2 deny rate increases by >2x baseline for any pilot org for 10m
- P1: evaluator timeout rate > 0.5% for 10m
- P1: authz p95 overhead > 5ms for 10m

Operational requirements
- All toggles must be dynamic config (no redeploy required).
- Maintain audit logging fields regardless of dual-read sampling decisions (audit is source of truth).
- Provide a single “rollback to v1” documented step for oncall.

Implementation plan
1) Define flags in shared config schema + plumb into gateway + control plane interceptors.
2) Implement dual-read decision compare utility in shared authz lib:
   - input: subject, action, scope, route, legacy_decision, v2_decision
   - output: metrics + structured log event
3) Wire diff telemetry emission in:
   - API Gateway middleware
   - Control plane request interceptor(s)
4) Create Datadog dashboards + monitors (coordinate with Logan Wright / Allison Grant for metric naming conventions).
5) Document rollout procedure in runbook and add “go/no-go” checklist.

Acceptance criteria
- Feature flags can be toggled at runtime in prod and verified via a test endpoint/health readout.
- Dual-read diff telemetry is emitted with stable cardinality (no unbounded tags).
- Dashboards available and reviewed by Security + Platform before first pilot.
- Alerting configured and validated in staging (simulate deny spike + evaluator failure).
- Rollback procedure tested (game day) with gateway + at least one control plane service.

Notes / open questions
- Cardinality control: avoid tagging by raw org_id on global dashboards; use sampled logs for per-org debugging, and only allow org-scoped metrics for pilot orgs via allowlist.
- Private deployments: do we ship default with v2_only disabled, dual_read disabled? Proposal: default to v1_only, customer can enable dual_read via config knob; Redwood SE helps flip to v2_only during pilot.
- Break-glass: ensure break-glass role bindings are unaffected by rollout toggles (i.e., break-glass works even if evaluator degraded). Needs explicit testing.

Links
- Related engineering tickets:
  - ENG-18277 gateway authorization middleware
  - ENG-18305 control plane permission annotations
  - ENG-18339 authz decision audit logging
- Related PRs (tracking):
  - PR: rbac-v2 feature flags + dual read (to be created)
  - PR: rollout dashboards + monitors (to be created)

Updates / comments
2025-03-01 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
- Drafted flag list + stage plan above. Aligning naming with Platform config conventions this week.
- Met with Logan/Allison on metric naming: will use prefix authz.rbacv2.* and keep tags limited to service, route_template, permission, decision, reason_code.

2025-03-08 (Amara Diallo)
- Gateway middleware already emits basic allow/deny counters; needs extension for dual-read diff metrics. Suggesting we emit diff only on mismatch to reduce volume.

2025-03-12 (Ethan Park)
- Control plane interceptor can compute legacy decision only for a subset of calls (some legacy checks are deep in handlers). Proposal: in those cases set legacy_decision=unknown and still emit v2 decision; rollout gating should be based on v2_unknown_rate (annotations) and explicit mismatch rates where legacy exists.

2025-03-18 (Marcus Lin)
- Security asks that we retain diff telemetry for at least first 30 days after GA for evidence during customer escalations. OK as long as sampling + cardinality controls are in place.

2025-03-22 (Connor O'Brien)
- Added due_date to align with pilot enablement window. Next step is a short review with Priya + Naomi to confirm Stage 2 criteria for Dedicated/Private.
